answer: One concrete defense is to give every agent a slow-growing reputation rooted in real work, like a juniper that takes seasons to mature. A newcomer may wander only inside a small circle of trusted peers, earning attestations one honest task at a time. A falcon cannot fake a long flight record: forged identities show thin histories, while genuine agents accumulate months of useful work that peers can verify. At each epoch the network promotes only those whose record checks out, so sybils stay quarantined at the edge and the cost of faking a credible identity keeps rising.
